verdict: Honeywell Aerospace's first quarter flying solo brought $4.6 billion of sales, $737 million of net income, a first-ever dividend, and a raised full-year outlook.

segments.name: Electronic Solutions
segments.note: Avionics and navigation electronics for aircraft and spacecraft — profit rose 11% as tariff refunds and pricing beat mix and costs.

segments.name: Engines and Power Systems
segments.note: Aircraft engines and power units; aftermarket volumes grew, but profit fell 16% on mix and higher costs.

segments.name: Control Systems
segments.note: Flight and engine control systems — sales were flat as defense and space growth offset a softer commercial aftermarket.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Developing new aerospace technology and products.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Sales, head office and new standalone-company costs after the spin-off.

otherDetail: Other income of $60M, less $187M of net interest expense on the debt issued for the separation — net −$127M.
footerNote: Operating income of $1,028M here is derived from the release's income statement (sales less cost of sales, R&D and SG&A); the company headlines a non-GAAP adjusted EBIT of $1.2B. Net income of $737M includes $11M attributable to noncontrolling interests; $726M was attributable to Honeywell Aerospace.

takeaways.title: A first dividend
takeaways.text: In its first quarter as a standalone company (spun off from Honeywell on June 29, 2026), Aerospace declared its inaugural quarterly dividend of $0.40 per share, payable December 4, 2026.

takeaways.title: Wins are stacking up
takeaways.text: The company has secured more than $20 billion of new wins (estimated lifetime value) year to date, with orders up 9% over the last 12 months — demand is not the problem; supplier output is.

takeaways.title: Two businesses, two directions
takeaways.text: Electronic Solutions' adjusted profit rose 11% while Engines and Power Systems fell 16% on unfavorable mix and higher costs — the quarter's story is which product line, not whether demand exists.

oneTimers: First quarter as a standalone public company: the balance sheet now carries $15.9 billion of long-term debt issued around the separation (versus $4M at the end of 2025), and results include incremental standalone corporate costs.
Prior-year figures are carve-out results from when Aerospace was part of Honeywell, and pre-spin EPS is calculated on the 317 million shares issued at the spin-off.
